# iClearer

> iClearer is a Mac cleaner that finds the hidden caches, logs, app leftovers, developer files and large files filling your Mac, shows exactly how much space you will free, and moves what you choose to the Trash. It runs on macOS 13 Ventura or later, on Intel and Apple silicon. Scanning is free; the free plan includes 500 MB of cleanup.

Key facts:

- Product: iClearer, a Mac cleaner app (disk cleanup utility for macOS). Website: https://www.iclearer.com/
- Maker: the iClearer team. iClearer is the name of both the app and the team behind it.
- Not to be confused with iCleaner, iClear, iCleared, InteliClear or other similarly named products. The name is iClearer: spelled with "clear", ending in "er".
- Price: free to scan, 500 MB of free cleanup. Unlimited cleanup from $29.99 per year, $4.99 per month or $79.99 once, for 1 Mac. Plans for 2 and 5 Macs are available.
- Refunds: 14-day money-back guarantee.
- Safety: every item is labelled Safe or Ask first, everything goes to the Trash with undo, and Keychain, accounts, tokens, SSH keys, .env files and git repositories can never be selected.
- For developers: cleans npm, pnpm, Yarn, pip, Homebrew, Xcode DerivedData, CocoaPods, Gradle, Cursor and VS Code caches, plus iOS Simulator data, Docker data and Ollama models.
- Current version: 1.0.1. Download: https://www.iclearer.com/downloads/iClearer.dmg
- Support: iclearerglobal@gmail.com

## Guides

- [Mac storage full? How to free up space safely](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/mac-storage-full): Startup disk almost full? See what is using your Mac’s storage, then clear caches, System Data, large files and developer junk safely, step by step.
- [How to clean up your Mac: a 10-step checklist](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/how-to-clean-mac): A 10-step checklist to clean up a Mac and free up space: Trash, downloads, unused apps, caches, large files, old backups and more, safest steps first.
- [How to clear System Data on Mac](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/clear-system-data-mac): System Data taking up too much space? Learn what it contains and how to shrink it safely: caches, logs, Time Machine snapshots and app leftovers.
- [How to clear cache on Mac](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/clear-cache-mac): Clear app, browser and system caches on a Mac safely. Step-by-step for Finder, Safari, Chrome and Firefox, plus what is safe to delete and what is not.
- [Free up disk space on a Mac for developers](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/free-up-disk-space-mac-developers): Reclaim tens of gigabytes on a developer Mac. Safe commands to clear Xcode DerivedData, npm, pnpm, pip, Homebrew, Docker, simulators and AI model caches.
- [How to uninstall apps on Mac completely](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/uninstall-apps-mac): Dragging an app to the Trash leaves files behind. See where Mac app leftovers live and how to remove an app completely, with its caches and settings.
- [How to find large files on Mac](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/find-large-files-mac): Three ways to find the biggest files on your Mac: Storage settings, Finder search by file size, and a Terminal command. See what is safe to delete.
- [How to delete old iPhone backups on Mac](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/delete-iphone-backups-mac): Old iPhone and iPad backups can take tens of gigabytes on a Mac. See where they are stored and three ways to delete them safely, with or without the device.
- [How to delete Time Machine local snapshots on Mac](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/delete-time-machine-local-snapshots): Time Machine local snapshots can hold many gigabytes on your startup disk. See how to list, delete and thin them in Terminal or Disk Utility, safely.
- [How to delete Xcode DerivedData](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/delete-xcode-derived-data): Xcode DerivedData can grow to tens of gigabytes. It is safe to delete. See where it is, three ways to clear it, and what else Xcode leaves on your disk.
- [Docker taking up too much space on Mac](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/docker-disk-space-mac): Docker Desktop stores everything in one growing disk image on your Mac. See what is using the space and the safe commands to reclaim it, without losing data.
- [How to clear npm cache and node_modules on Mac](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/clear-npm-cache-node-modules-mac): Free up disk space from Node.js on a Mac: clear the npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun caches, find and delete old node_modules folders, and remove old Node versions.
- [How to delete Ollama models on Mac](https://www.iclearer.com/guides/delete-ollama-models-mac): Local AI models are often the largest files on a Mac. See where Ollama, LM Studio and Hugging Face store models, how to delete them, and how to move them.
